text:
Alex: PR #8429 up for quick review — changes to allocator scheduling + a new prefill_compaction heuristic intended to reduce peak memory. Quick summary from local bench (4k tokens, 200 runs): p95 ~+8% vs main, throughput +3%, mem_peak -15%. Need two approvals before merge. Bench artifacts: https://gist.github.com/redwood/8429-bench

Sam: can you paste the commit and the exact bench command? Also was preemption disabled?

Lina: Commit 9f4b2a3. Bench command used: ```./bench --model redwood-4k --runs=200 --batch=8 --seq=4096 --env=dedicated-small --preemption=false``` Results summary: ```p50 30ms | p95 180ms (main 167ms) | p99 340ms (main 320ms) | tput 2100 tok/s (main 2050) | mem_peak 42GB (main 50GB)```

Morgan: interesting — mem win is nice but tail bump sucks. Did you try toggling the new prefill_compaction flag?

Alex: not yet, will run that next. Holding on merge until we get quick eyes + a canary. If we don't get 2 approvals in ~6h I'll revert the prefill_compaction part.

devops-bot: Canary deploy triggered for pr-8429 on cluster us-west-2a (10 nodes). Canary window: 6h.

Sara: I kicked off a heatmap on the canary. Small batches look fine overall but ~1% of runs show p99 spikes to ~450ms. Snapshot uploaded to the artifacts link.

Tyler: my hunch — allocator fast-path changed allocation order, causing occasional refill jitter/lock contention. Try adding a 2ms jitter before refill to see if that smooths the tail.

Lina: reran with prefill_compaction=false and refill_jitter=2ms. New results: ```p50 31ms | p95 168ms | p99 325ms | tput 2080 tok/s | mem_peak 49GB``` That pushes p95/p99 back near main while mostly preserving the mem reduction.

Morgan: that isolates it nicely. Recommend splitting the work: keep the scheduler changes (smaller risk) and revert or move prefill_compaction to a follow-up PR with more tests. We'll need 2 approvals for the scheduler PR.

Alex: split into #8429 (scheduler) and #8430 (prefill_compaction). Can we get reviews on 8429? @Sam @Sara @Tyler please double-check.

Sam: I'll review this afternoon.

Sara: LGTM for 8429 pending a tiny doc note about the scheduler heuristic. Happy to approve after that.

Tyler: +1 on 8429, will approve once CI is green.

Alex: thanks all. Leaving canary running for the 6h window; will merge 8429 after two approvals + green canary. If we see regressions, we'll revert via canary bot and follow up on 8430.
